# dsh-codex-memories
Codex-style **long-term memory** for DSH: cross-session memory that ingests finished sessions, conso
lidates them into a searchable handbook, and injects a compact summary before every turn.
It reproduces the two-stage structure of the Codex memory system rather than approximating it: per-s
ession extraction first, then a consolidation pass over many raw memories.
## Why
DSH sessions are isolated by default. A correction you made yesterday, a command that only works in
one repo, a symptom/cause/fix you already paid for — none of it carries over unless you restate it.
This plugin makes the agent remember:

- how you want it to work, without being told twice
- where the truth lives in a specific repo, and

which commands actually run
- which failure has which fix

| Tool | Effect |
| `memory_search` | line-level keyword search across memory files (`any` / `all` / `on_same_line`) |

| `memory_read` | read one memory file by line range |
| `memory_list` | inventory of the memory fo

lder and pending work |
| `memory_note` | append one ad-hoc note — the only write path the model is

pending work |
| `memory_note` | append one ad-hoc note — the only write path the model is offered |
The model is instructed to cite memory as `MEMORY.md:12-14|note=[...]`.

## Cost and privacy
- **It spends tokens**: one Stage-1 call per session and one Stage-2 call per consolidation. Session

s under 4 messages are skipped; at most 3 sessions are processed per sweep.
- **Local files only**:

no network access beyond the model API it calls.
- **It enters your prompt**: `memory_summary.md` is

injected every turn, which is why it is capped by `maxInjectChars`.
- **Auditable**: every artifact

is readable Markdown.
- **The model cannot rewrite the handbook**: it may only append ad-hoc notes;
consolidation is a separate pass, so one turn cannot corrupt durable memory.
## Fidelity to Codex
The behavioral spec comes from reverse engineering Codex itself — the on-disk shape under `~/.codex/
memories` plus the prompt templates embedded in `codex.exe`:
| Codex | dsh-codex-memories |

| `~/.codex/memories/` | `$DSH_HOME/memories/` |
| `MEMORY.md` / `memory_summary.md` / `raw_memories

.md` | same names, same formats |
| `rollout_summaries/*.md` | `session_summaries/*.md` |
| `memorie

s_1.sqlite` | `index.json` |
| Stage 1 extraction prompt | `PHASE1_TEMPLATE` in `lib/prompts.js` |
|

Phase 2 consolidation prompt | `PHASE2_TEMPLATE` in `lib/prompts.js` |
| usage guidance + citation

format | `USAGE_TEMPLATE` in `lib/prompts.js` |
| rollout scan backfill | `/memory backfill` + boot

| `USAGE_TEMPLATE` in `lib/prompts.js` |
| rollout scan backfill | `/memory backfill` + boot sweep |
See docs/mechanism.md for the full mechanism and the evidence behind it.
## Known limits
- Stage 2 asks for two complete documents in one reply. On a very large handbook the reply can hit t
he output cap; the old files are then kept and the pass reports an error instead of writing somethin

g corrupt.
- Automatic extraction needs the process alive during the idle window; otherwise the next

boot's `backfill` catches up.
- Retrieval is keyword/line based, not semantic — the same tradeoff C
odex makes. Route with `keywords` in `MEMORY.md`.
## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see CONTRIBUTING.md. For anything
security-related, follow SE

CURITY.md instead of opening a public issue. Release
history lives in CHANGELOG.md.
